answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the result efficiently. GPUs may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot collapse the dependency steps within a chain, so every clone still incurs the full time delay. This makes Sybil identities costly to obtain quickly—not impossible—and gives copper, nectar, and ripple no computational shortcut.
